response.query: How can Neyman or optimal allocation be applied to assign clusters and student counts across strata to minimize variance for the primary estimand?
response.answer: Neyman allocation assigns samples to strata based on their population size and standard deviation to minimize variance. It prioritizes strata with higher variability. When costs vary, cost-optimal allocation adjusts for this.

results.title: Neyman Optimal Allocation Calculator | MetricGate
results.content: Neyman optimal allocation is the gold standard for distributing a fixed total sample across strata in a stratified survey. Proposed by Jerzy Neyman in 1934, it assigns sample to each stratum in proportion to its population size times its standard deviation — concentrating effort where variability is greatest — and thereby minimizes the variance of the stratified mean estimator for a given total n. * **Cost extension:** When sampling costs differ, cost-optimal allocation weights by N\_h S\_h / \sqrt{C\_h}, minimizing variance for a fixed budget. When all strata have equal variability, Neyman allocation collapses to proportional allocation and the two methods are equivalent. When per-unit cost C\_h varies by stratum, the **cost-optimal allocation** minimizes variance for a fixed total cost C = \sum n\_h C\_h:. Neyman optimal allocation is a method for distributing a fixed total sample size n across strata in a stratified survey to minimize the variance of the population mean estimator.

results.title: Neyman allocation - Wikipedia
results.content: # Neyman allocation. Method of sample size allocation. **Neyman allocation**, also known as optimum allocation, is a method of sample size allocation in stratified sampling developed by Jerzy Neyman in 1934. This technique determines the optimal sample size for each stratum to minimize the variance of the estimated population parameter for a fixed total sample size and cost. Neyman allocation determines the sample size *nh* for each stratum *h* that minimizes the variance of the estimated population mean or total. The Neyman allocation formula is:. * *nh* is the sample size for stratum *h*. * *n* is the total sample size. * *Nh* is the population size for stratum *h*. The derivation of Neyman allocation follows from minimizing the variance of the stratified mean estimator subject to a fixed total sample size constraint. Using the method of Lagrange multipliers to minimize this variance subject to the constraint Σ*nh* = *n* leads to the Neyman allocation formula.

results.content: Optimal Allocation refers to the allocation of sample sizes across strata in a way that minimizes the variance of estimated population parameters. It aims to provide more precise parameter estimates compared to simple random sampling or proportional allocation, by sampling strata in proportion to their standard deviations and population fractions. :   The allocation of a sample to strata in a way that does not reflect the actual proportion of the strata in the population; also known as oversampling. :   The allocation of a sample to strata in a way that minimizes the variance of estimated population parameters; in some cases known as Neyman allocation. :   The allocation of a sample to strata in proportion to the actual proportion of the strata in the population. *An optimal portfolio allocation strategy is*. results.title: Sage Research Methods - Encyclopedia of Survey Research Methods - Neyman Allocation
results.content: Neyman allocation assigns sample units within each stratum proportional to the product of the population stratum size (Nh) and the within-stratum standard deviation (Sh), so that minimum variance for a population mean estimator can be achieved. If the variances are uniform across all the strata as well, Neyman allocation reduces to proportional allocation where the number of sampled units in each stratum is proportional to the population size of the stratum.
